local_entities.label: Human descendants on the Delta Quadrant planet

evidence.summary: Voyager follows rust and an SOS signal to a planet and lands because atmospheric interference prevents transport or safe shuttle access.
The crew finds eight living humans in functioning cryostasis, including a woman identified from clothing and records as Amelia Earhart.
Earhart and others report being taken from Earth by an unexplained light in 1937.
evidence.counterevidence: The testimony establishes their recollection, while later descendant testimony supplies a separate historical account.

evidence.summary: Evansville states that the Briori abducted hundreds of humans in 1937, enslaved them, and were overthrown by the captives' descendants.
evidence.counterevidence: This is a descendant historical account rather than independently recovered Briori documentation.

evidence.summary: Janeway considers whether Voyager should continue home when the crew is offered settlement on a thriving human world, then allows each crew member to choose.
The revived 1937 abductees choose to remain with their descendants; Voyager prepares to depart after no crew member chooses settlement.

assertions.subject: voy-37:37s
counterevidence: Different parts of the history are supported by survivor recollection and descendant testimony rather than a single independent record.

assertions.subject: voy-37:janeway
assertions.object: remain on human colony or continue home

neutral_coding.plot_problem: A possible route-home clue instead reveals abducted 20th-century humans and a mature descendant civilization.
neutral_coding.epistemics: Personal recollection, descendant history, sensor evidence, and inference are kept separate.
neutral_coding.agency: Janeway permits individual crew choice rather than unilaterally deciding settlement.
neutral_coding.counterevidence: The Briori abduction/slavery history is not independently verified by a surviving Briori record in this work.
